_readme: Every Penny release, newest first. Add one with ./penny release <version> --summary "..." [--note "..."] [--required]. A required release is the minimum: older copies must update before real runs or changes. Versions before 1.6.0 had no update checks, so none of them is required.

releases.summary: A profile each person manages: details, photo, password and private activity
notes: My profile, in the menu under your name: change your name, title, about line, who covers for you, and your photo. Your username and user ID stay the same.
Change your password while signed in. Your other devices are signed out.
My activity shows your own numbers. Only you can see them.

releases.summary: A guided tour, a case study, a getting started guide and screenshots
notes: Take the tour: nine stops on the real pages, in about two minutes. Find it at the top of the Overview, in the Help center, and in the menu under your name. It changes nothing.
A getting started guide for anyone who downloads the project, and a short case study, both on GitHub.

releases.summary: The left menu scrolls, so Help center is never cut off
notes: The left menu now scrolls by itself when the window is too short to show every link. Before, Help center could sit below the bottom of the screen.
On phones the menu uses the height of the visible screen, so the browser's bars no longer hide the last link.

releases.summary: Penny is a portfolio project, not production software. The help center now says what production would take, and names sign-in with Microsoft and Google as the next step.
notes: New help article: Is Penny ready for production?
Sign-in with Microsoft and Google is the next thing planned.
No change to how Penny works.

releases.summary: The reasons behind Penny's design are now in the help center: a Decisions and why article, and a note on each feature saying why it works the way it does.
notes: New help article: Decisions and why.
A "Why it works this way" note on 25 help articles.
No change to how Penny works.

releases.summary: A setup wizard: double-click Install Penny, answer five screens in your browser, and Penny is ready for you or your team.
notes: Install Penny (Mac and Windows) installs Penny and opens the wizard. No commands to type.
The wizard checks this computer, finds your invoice package, sets up who signs in, and saves a few settings.
Start Penny starts it the way the wizard was told to.
The wizard is closed unless Penny itself opens it.

releases.summary: Security fixes from a review of 2.0, including a way around sign-in. Update now if Penny runs with real accounts.
notes: Fixed: with real accounts on, invoices and files could be downloaded without signing in by spelling the address another way. This was in every version since 1.7.
Penny on one computer now only answers to that computer's own address.
Every field of an action is checked before it is saved, so one browser cannot break a page for the team.
Work moved in from a browser never counts as an approval, an import or a second check.
Wrong-password limits work properly behind a proxy, and error details stay in the terminal.

releases.summary: Penny for a real team: one server checks and saves everyone's work, teammates see it live, and Penny can run over a network with https.
notes: With real accounts, everything people do is saved on the server, not in each browser. Sign in anywhere and your work is there.
Live updates: a teammate's work shows up without a reload, and two people cannot resolve the same hold at once.
The server checks every action: your role, what teammates already did, and second-person rules.
Rule changes made on the Rules page are the rules Penny runs with.
The audit log lives in a database that refuses changes and deletions.
Run for a team with ./penny web --host 0.0.0.0 --https. Penny refuses the network without real accounts and https.
Older files are moved into the database the first time 2.0 starts. Nothing is deleted.
The public demo is unchanged.

releases.summary: Made for phones: lists become cards, buttons are thumb sized, filters fold away and dialogs rise from the bottom.
notes: On a phone, each invoice is a card with the vendor and amount side by side. Nothing scrolls sideways.
Buttons and fields are at least 44 pixels tall on touch screens, and tapping a field no longer zooms the page.
Filters on Invoices fold behind one button. Dialogs rise from the bottom of the screen.
Nothing changes on a computer.

releases.summary: See where each value came from on the PDF, track each import file so nothing is imported twice, a watched folder, paging for long lists, and an accessibility pass.
notes: Show on page: highlight on the PDF where Penny read each value.
Export history: Created, Downloaded, Imported and Confirmed for the Intacct and Entrata files, with a row count check and a second person.
Watched folder: drop PDFs into inbox/_incoming and Penny previews them. It never runs a batch for real.
Long lists show 25 rows at a time and stay quick with thousands of invoices.
Accessibility: every screen checked against WCAG 2.2 AA, with fixes for links, the skip link, phones, tables and contrast.

releases.summary: A stronger foundation: browser tests on every change, a faster server, a content security policy, and clearer code. No new features.
notes: The browser tests are now part of the project and run on every pull request.
Faster: files are fingerprinted once, and only new audit log lines and changed files are read.
Safer: a content security policy, fonts bundled so nothing loads from other sites, and safer response headers.
Clearer: the web app is 13 files by area, and every function has a short description.

releases.summary: Admins manage people with invitations, roles and password resets; exports and approval requests can be emailed; everyone can choose how Penny looks.
notes: Users page for Admins: invite someone, change roles and details, turn accounts off and on, resend invitations and send password resets.
Invitation and reset links work once and expire. Forgot your password? is on the sign-in page.
On a computer, accounts are real once the first Admin is invited with ./penny users invite, and Penny sends real email through your mail account.
Email any export, or a bill for approval, with the file attached. Only Penny users and your company's domains can be emailed. Every email is in the Outbox.
Appearance: seven preset themes or any custom color (kept readable), light or dark, text size, density and motion. Admins set the company look.

releases.summary: Penny shows its version on every screen and tells you when a new one is ready, required or optional.
notes: The version is at the bottom of every screen, with a What's new page.
When a new version is ready, Penny says so. You can update now, read what is new, or skip an optional version until the next one.
A required version pauses real runs and changes until you update. Reading results, help, previews and rechecks keep working.
In the terminal: ./penny --version, ./penny update, and ./penny update --skip.
Every run records the Penny version that made its decisions.

releases.summary: Blockers, recheck previews, a rule simulator, manual entry with a second-person check, and a most-urgent-first queue.
notes: Each reason for a hold is a blocker with an owner, a target date, notes and fingerprinted files.
Recheck decides a held invoice again without saving anything, and Test on saved invoices shows what a rule change would do.
Files Penny cannot read can be keyed by hand beside a screenshot; above a limit, a second person checks the entry.
My work shows the most urgent holds first and says why.

releases.summary: Upload and run new batches from the web app, suggested fixes that learn, usage insights, and every rule editable.
Sign-in with four roles, real actions, an audit trail, a rules editor, a redesigned interface and a help center.
A web view in the browser, read only.
A bad or unreadable file is held with a clear reason instead of stopping the run.
The Hillpointe AP technical screen, as submitted.
